answer: A reputation bond that melts like a glacier works well: each agent must lock a stake that thaws slowly over weeks, so creating many fake identities ties up real capital per identity. Honest work earns nectar-like micro-rewards that accumulate only with a long history of verified tasks, while a new identity starts with none. Sybil identities therefore face a slow river of costs: the stake lockup, the time to build reputation, and forfeiture of the bond if peers attest fraud, making mass fake identities far more expensive than the rewards they could harvest.
